title: Give the important moment a beautifully simple setting
intro: A proposal dinner in Dubai needs food and service that support the moment you are planning. The strongest brief starts with the setting, the timing of the proposal and how much you want your partner to know beforehand. myCHEF can discuss the dining element and any requested coordination within the agreed scope. This guide helps you think through the surprise, menu and practical responsibilities so the evening has a clear plan behind it while still feeling personal and unforced.

sections.title: Keep one clear plan behind the surprise
paragraphs: Choose a designated contact for discreet questions and tell the team when normal conversation or service should pause. If you are arranging a photographer, musician or flowers, connect their timing to the same plan rather than treating each element separately.

A backup for timing changes is useful too. Guests may arrive later than expected or you may prefer to wait for a more natural moment. Discuss how the dining service can respond within the booked hours. Clear preparation gives you more freedom to enjoy the occasion without directing every detail in front of your partner.

sections.title: Protect the surprise with a simple timing plan
paragraphs: A proposal dinner works best when the important moment has space around it. Decide whether the proposal will happen before the meal, between courses or after dessert, then tell the coordinator what should pause and what should continue. The fewer people who need to improvise on the day, the easier it is to keep the experience calm.

Agree how the team should communicate without revealing the surprise. A designated contact and a clear signal are often more practical than a long sequence of last-minute messages. If a photographer, musician or florist is involved, their arrival and setup need to fit the same schedule and the property's access rules.

The food should suit both guests and the setting. Share preferences discreetly, including any dietary requirements, and keep the menu manageable for the available kitchen. Confirm which extras are included and which you are organising yourself. Thoughtful coordination lets the occasion feel personal while keeping the responsibilities behind it clear.

sections.title: Create an intimate dinner with room to be yourselves
paragraphs: For dinner for two, personal details often matter more than the number of courses. A favourite ingredient, a dish linked to a shared memory or a relaxed serving pace can make the evening feel considered. Tell us whether you want a quiet meal with discreet service or a more interactive experience with the chef explaining each course.

Choose a menu that leaves room for conversation. You may prefer a few beautifully balanced courses to a long sequence that repeatedly interrupts the evening. Discuss when you would like the chef and any service staff present, and when you would prefer more privacy. The kitchen and table layout will help determine what is practical.

Flowers, table styling and other extras should be included in the proposal if you want them arranged. If you have a surprise planned, identify one contact and a simple communication plan. Clear preparation behind the scenes allows the dinner itself to feel natural, without turning a personal occasion into a complicated production.

sections.title: Make the table work as well as it looks
paragraphs: A beautiful table should still leave room to eat comfortably. Consider the number of plates, glasses and serving dishes before deciding on flowers or decorative pieces. A sharing menu needs space in the centre; a plated menu may need room for several pieces of cutlery or a separate bread plate. The menu and table layout should be planned together.

Check what is available at the property and what needs to be arranged. Crockery, serving platters, linen and glassware are not interchangeable with kitchen equipment, and they should not be assumed to be included unless your proposal says so. Tell the team if you want a particular style, colour palette or level of formality.

Lighting and access matter, too. Guests need to see the food, and staff need a safe route between the table and kitchen. A simple, thoughtfully arranged setting can feel more welcoming than an overcrowded display. Confirm setup and clear-down responsibilities so the presentation remains practical throughout the occasion.

sections.title: Choose courses that belong together
paragraphs: A memorable dinner menu is more than a list of favourite dishes. Think about how the courses follow one another: a fresh beginning, a satisfying main course and a finish that complements what came before. Repeating the same rich ingredient or cooking style throughout can make a meal feel heavier than intended, even when each dish is good on its own.

Share your must-have dishes and let the chef recommend the supporting courses. If a particular main course is the centrepiece, the starter and dessert can be chosen to balance it. The menu should also respect the kitchen and service team, especially when several plates need to reach the table together.

Consider the pace you want. A relaxed family gathering, a birthday dinner and an interactive tasting menu may all use different course structures. Agreeing the format early makes it easier to discuss portions, staffing and timing. The most persuasive menu is one that sounds enjoyable to your guests and can be delivered comfortably in the setting.

sections.title: Set expectations for discretion in your home
paragraphs: Inviting a chef into your home involves more than sharing a kitchen. Explain any household boundaries before the visit: rooms that are private, preferred routes through the property and how to communicate while you are working or entertaining. Practical instructions make it easier for the service to fit naturally into your day.

Photography should be discussed separately from cooking. If your household does not want photographs taken, say so clearly in the brief. Any request to share images of a booking should be handled with the relevant permission; a meal at home is not automatically a marketing opportunity. You can also raise any specific confidentiality requirements before confirming the arrangement.

Keep sensitive details proportionate to what is needed for the service. Menus, allergies and arrival instructions help the chef do the job; unrelated personal information usually does not. Your myCHEF contact can help clarify how a privacy request affects the booking and which details need to be passed to the proposed professional.

sections.title: Confirm the practical details before the date is secured
paragraphs: A promising menu is only one part of a booking. Before confirming, review the date, address, guest count, arrival time, service hours and included roles. Make sure the dietary brief and any essential equipment requirements are reflected in the proposal rather than left in separate messages that can be overlooked.

Read the payment schedule and the terms that apply to your particular service. A recurring household plan and a one-off event may have different arrangements for changes, cancellation and outstanding balances. Use the terms attached to your booking rather than assuming a policy from another service or an earlier quotation automatically applies.

Keep one agreed version of the menu and scope. If you change the number of guests, request a new dish or move the meal time, ask for confirmation of any effect on staffing, availability and price. This creates a clear reference for you and the team and helps the chef prepare for the service you actually expect.
